articles.title_orig: Live Updates: Russian foreign minister says he's visiting Iran for talks to avert return to "large-scale war"
articles.title_zh: Live Updates: Russian foreign minister says he's visiting Iran for talks to avert return to "large-scale war"
articles.content_orig:
Egypt's parliament on Monday postponed its debate on President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi's request to authorize military support to Saudi Arabia, which has faced mounting attacks from Yemen's Houthis, Egyptian state media reported. The debate has been delayed until next week, according to the report.
"House Speaker Hisham Badawi has adjourned the second parliamentary session dedicated to discussing authorisation for taking necessary measures to support and assist the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, with discussions set to resume on October 26," Egypt's state-run Al-Akhbar newspaper reported.
The postponement concluded a second day of parliamentary sessions in which Egyptian lawmakers weighed Sisi's request to approve support for Saudi Arabia, if requested by the kingdom. An emergency session on Sunday also ended without a decision.
Two lawmakers told AFP on Sunday that most parliamentarians supported the proposal, and a decision wasn't reached during that first session in order to "give all lawmakers the opportunity to speak and express their views."
The Egyptian Social Democratic Party, an opposition party with nearly a dozen seats in parliament, said it had instructed its parliamentary bloc to abstain from voting.
Although it described its solidarity with Saudi Arabia as "firm," the party said any deployment of Egyptian forces abroad should be guided by "specific objectives, clear information" and "an accurate assessment of the potential risks to the lives of our soldiers."
Yemen's Saudi-backed government claimed Monday to have killed 558 Houthi fighters over the past 24 hours. In a post on X , Col. Majed Al-Nazili said Yemeni forces had carried out 1,164 operations against the Iran-backed rebels.
"The operations resulted in neutralizing (558) militia elements, including field commanders," he wrote.
A major Saudi investment conference is set to be postponed, three sources briefed on the matter told the French news agency AFP on Monday, amid repeated attacks on the kingdom by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels .
One source said the event "won't happen on time" and that organizers "won't announce a new date soon." A second source, who confirmed the event would be postponed, told AFP: "Who would be willing to risk flying to Riyadh these days?"
Saudi Arabia's Future Investment Initiative (FII) Institute hosts an annual forum often referred to as "Davos in the desert." The event typically draws foreign leaders and business titans, and this year it is  scheduled to be held in Riyadh from Oct. 26 to 29.
The Wall Street Journal reported that the conference would either be held online or postponed.
Iran's top diplomat on Monday accused the United States of being responsible for the insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz that has left the nearly-eight month conflict sparked by joint U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran unresolved, despite the cessation of major military operations.
"The war imposed by the United States and the Zionist regime [Israel], combined with the economic blockade [on Iran's ports], constitutes the principal source of insecurity in our region," said Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, echoing many similar statements by himself and other senior Iranian figures.
He made the remark Monday during a joint news conference with his Russian counterpart Sergey Lavrov, who arrived in Tehran earlier Monday for his first visit since the outbreak of the war, as Russia tries to frame itself as a potential mediator despite close ties with the Iranian regime.
Lavrov was also scheduled to meet Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian during his visit, according to Russia's foreign ministry. The veteran Russian diplomat said Moscow's efforts were "aimed at preventing the return of a large-scale war," with talks between Tehran and Washington at a standstill.
Iran's Acting Oil Minister Hamid Bovard met Qatar's Minister of State for Energy Affairs, Saad Sherida al-Kaabi, in Doha on Monday to discuss energy relations and cooperation between the two countries.
According to Iran's official news agency IRNA , al-Kaabi confirmed the meeting, which focused on bilateral energy ties and opportunities for cooperation.
The death toll from a Houthi missile strike on a camp in Yemen's government-controlled Shabwa province rose to 50 on Monday, a government official told the French news agency AFP, after military sources earlier put the toll at more than 30.
The Iran-backed rebels fired ballistic missiles at the al-Alam military camp in the southern province of Shabwa.
"The death toll has risen to at least 50, with more than 100 people injured, some of them in critical condition," said Fahad al-Khalifi, deputy governor of Shabwa.
He added that hospitals in the province were overwhelmed and had been forced to transfer the most seriously wounded to facilities in neighbouring Hadramout and Aden.
Iran-backed Houthi rebels struck a military camp for government forces in southern Yemen on Monday, killing at least 20 soldiers, two Yemeni military officials said.
The rebels fired ballistic missiles at the al-Alam military camp in the southern province of Shabwa in an attack that left at least two dozen more troops wounded, the officials said.
The military officials with the internationally recognized government of Yemen spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to brief the media.
Yemen's decade-long civil war has intensified and become intertwined with the wider regional conflict sparked by the U.S. war with Iran over the last few months, as the Houthis, considered one of Iran's most potent proxy forces, attacks the government's Saudi backers on their home turf.
Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure, including civilian airports, have killed more than 20 people in recent weeks, and President Trump has said he's considering joining Saudi operations against the rebels. The Houthis have warned that if the U.S. does intervene, it would prompt a  "swift and painful" retaliation against U.S. personnel and interests across the region.
Oil prices were down early Monday, with Brent crude, the international standard, falling 2.5% to $107.16 per barrel and benchmark U.S. crude dropping 2.2% to $96.84 per barrel.
The prices fell after President Trump late Friday signed an executive order to put new U.S. sanctions against Russia on hold just days before they were to come into effect, drawing disappointment from Ukraine , with the move likely resulting in more energy exports from Russia.
Mr. Trump's decision came not long after he said earlier this month he had reached a diesel deal with Russia in an attempt to bring down elevated U.S. fuel prices ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections.
But despite Mr. Trump's controversial efforts to ease energy costs for Americans, oil prices have remained much higher compared to before the Iran war, due in large part to the ongoing risks to the supply chain caused by the crisis in the Middle East .
On Friday the price of Brent crude hit nearly $110 a barrel, its highest level since mid-May.
A tug boat traveling near the Strait of Hormuz was struck by two unknown projectiles, a British maritime monitoring agency said Sunday .
The U.K. navy's Maritime Trade Operations center (UKMTO) said in a statement that a tugboat traveling southbound off the coast of the United Arab Emirates "reported being struck by two unknown projectiles."
"The tug has sustained damage but is continuing on its route," the agency said, "one minor casualty has been reported."
Last week saw 10 attacks on commercial vessels in and near the strait, according to the UKMTO, which said October has already become the worst month for attacks on shipping in the strait since the early days of the war in March.
The U.S. issued a security alert on Monday urging Americans in the Middle East to "exercise heightened vigilance."

articles.title_zh: Gangs in Haiti target foreign troops in biggest attack since new force began operations
articles.content_orig:
More than 200 mostly young people said to be injured after ballistic missile attack on training camp for government forces
At least 53 people have been killed in a Houthi ballistic missile attack on a training camp for Yemeni government forces, making it the largest single loss of life since the country’s civil war reignited in September.
The attack on al-Alam camp in the southern Shabwa province was said to have injured more than 200 others, mostly young recruits, and described as a disaster by the country’s UN-recognised government. The injured were taken from the police and army training camp in the Jardan district to a hospital in the local capital, Ataq, where pleas for blood donations were made.
There will be an inquiry into how so many troops were left so exposed to a Houthi attacks. In mid-September, the group began a fresh push on forces backing the UN-recognised government by pushing south along the Red Sea coast to try to take control of the Bab al-Mandab waterway.
Reliable assessments of the death toll in the fighting over the last month are hard to gather, but it is running into the many thousands. A Saudi airstrike on Sunday killed nine, including five children and two women.
Rashad al-Alimi, the president of the UN-recognised government, said those killed on Monday were new recruits, and he vowed an immediate hard response. He said the incident “affirmed that targeting the recruits reflects the Houthi militias’ approach of resorting to cowardly terrorist attacks whenever they face pressures or their Iranian-backed sabotage plots falter”.
He had already on Monday phoned the UN secretary general, António Guterres, to ask for the UN to classify the Houthis as a foreign terrorist organisation.
The Shabwa provincial authority said: “Targeting recruits constitutes a military escalation and a blatant assault on the province’s security.” Its governor, Awad bin Al-Wazir, visited the wounded in hospitals.
The killings underline the dangers of large numbers of troops gathering in one place within reach of the Houthi ballistic missile arsenal. The training camp was struck by three ballistic missiles while the recruits lined up in formation.
Houthi forces have also cut the road between government-run Shabwa and the Houthi-run Bayda governorate.
The Houthi military spokesperson said: “Our armed forces targeted the Saudi enemy’s mobilisations in the Al-Alam camp, which is run by Saudi officers in the eastern regions. The targeting resulted in the fall of dozens of dead and wounded from the Saudi enemy’s mobilizations, including Saudi officers.
“We warn the deceived ones against responding to the Saudi enemy’s calls to lure them with his defiled money to the pyres of death, and to exploit them instead of his soldiers who are indifferent to their lives.”
Fighting is also under way as Houthis try to mount a siege of the Yemeni city Taiz, and citizens have been calling for greater air protection.
Southern forces were said to be making progress in edging Houthi forces out of control of the area around the Bab al-Mandab, the narrowest waterway taking ships from the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean.
It is not clear whether the Houthis have decided to slow the pace of attacks on Saudi airports and energy installations, or they are running low on munitions.
The Saudi Armaco headquarters was struck last weekend and some airlines have said they are not yet going to resume using Riyadh airport. The airport formally reopened at the weekend after being attacked this month .
Hans Grundberg, the UN envoy for Yemen, is due in London to meet ministers on Tuesday.

articles.title_orig: Unprecedented Collab Between China and the Met Uncovers Secrets of Chinese Mural During Exhaustive Reproduction
articles.title_zh: Unprecedented Collab Between China and the Met Uncovers Secrets of Chinese Mural During Exhaustive Reproduction
articles.content_orig:
A major arts and heritage conservation project in China has born unexpected fruit thousands of miles away in New York City.
In the Chinese arts and antiquities gallery of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, a 50-foot-long mural devours the attention of an entire room with its arrangement of Buddha and his attendants.
The Medicine Buddha mural had long attracted the wonder of Zhang Jian, director of the “Meticulous Painting Institute” at the Chinese National Academy of Arts, which since 2013 has poured billions of Chinese RMB into restoring, conserving, and repatriating Chinese artifacts around the country and the world.
Describing it as wielding an “awe-inspiring energy,” Zhang learned that the mural was originally located in the ancient Guangsheng Temple in central China. Standing in its halls years later, staring at the vacant space where the massive mural had originally hung, Zhang was struck with an idea.
Over the next 3 years, he led a team of special artists and conservationists to the Met to meticulously—excruciatingly—copy the mural for a life-sized replica that captures every single crack, faded contour, and conservationist correction it had faced in its 700 years on the Earth.
This project was made possible with the unerring support of the Met itself, a collaboration which marks arguably the highest ever undertaken between Chinese and American cultural institutes.
Now in October, the Met is to co-host an international symposium in Beijing about Chinese murals, marking the first time the New York museum has jointly held a major academic conference in China with a national research body.
Jason Sun, the Met’s curator of Chinese art, told the South China Morning Post that the results achieved by Zhang’s team—including the realization that conservators had incorrectly arranged the mural segments so that Lord Buddha’s head was 2 centimeters off kilter—as having “profound historical and practical significance.”
Painted around 700 years ago during the Mongol-administered Yuan Dynasty, on clay tiles mixed with rice straw, the mural depicts the Medicine Buddha seated with his chief attendants surrounded by numerous figures.
Yet its presence in the Met isn’t the result of it being a plundered relic. Mainland China was mostly free from Western colonial occupation when the impoverished monks from Guangsheng Temple chopped the mural up into sections and sold it to fix the collapsing roof of their temple.
Among the keystones of Buddha’s teachings is the unavoidable truth that all things are impermanent, so if they were good students of the Great Sage, those impoverished monks would not have hesitated to part with the relic, that traded hands across the West until it arrived at the Met via donation from Arthur Sackler in 1965.
The China National Arts Fund, a state-endowed philanthropic fund established in 2013 under the National Academy of Arts, was as recently as 2025 tasked specifically with the preservation of ancient murals and other works. So far, 40 ancient murals from caves and temples across Western China have been painstakingly examined and copied, but if they are held overseas, the Fund has the directive to pay for their study, and potentially, their recreation.
Yet Zhang had a different sort of intention for that recreation: one that the Met administrators enthusiastically supported. In 2024, SCMP reports that the Fund had formalized a research partnership with the Met, whereby the famous museum granted their colleagues in East Asia full authorization for prolonged detailed study of the work, and the sharing of ultra-high-resolution digital images.
CHINESE MURALS IN THE NEWS: Stunning Tang Dynasty Mural Unearthed in China Portrays a ‘Westerner’ with Blonde Hair
“The Met staff actively coordinated with visitors for us,” said Meng Ying, an artist on Zhang’s team which visited the Met 3 times over the following years. “Though our lifts and lighting equipment occasionally blocked sightlines, visitors were remarkably understanding.”
As Meng said, studying portions of the work required specialized hydraulic lifts and expansive light fixtures, conditions which he described as being “unprecedented” in the history of the Met. This went on for days at a time, while the team poured their attention onto the smallest details to reproduce exactly what it was that the Guangsheng Temple was missing.
This included using clay-rich mud and rice straw to make the tiles, which they sourced from as close to the temple as possible. It involved extensive studying into the mineral pigments—considering what would have been available to the medieval painters, and how such materials could have changed over 700 years.
“Lighting, digital cameras ,and printing all change how a color looks. We had to tweak our paints over and over again on site,” said Han Maoyuan, another artist on the team.
MORE COLLABORATION LIKE THIS: Since 1968 French Teachers Have Come to Louisiana Classrooms to Preserve French Language Through Immersion
Yet further, the team layered their mud tiles to create a base-layer painting and a second to replicate the scars left by time and intervention.
As mentioned earlier, the team’s exhaustive examination of the mural revealed that its original mounters in the Met’s galleries had misunderstood Chinese brushwork, and misaligned the Buddha’s head by 2 centimeters. Met staff told SCMP that after the disbelief wore off, they couldn’t walk through the room without noticing that the Buddha’s head was crooked.
The finished mural produced by Zhang and his team made its public debut at the China National Arts and Crafts Museum in Beijing, where on September 24th, in honor of President Xi Jinping’s visit to the US, an exhibition was held featuring the fruits of the National Art Fund’s preservation and reproduction efforts.
FROM THE MET: Rare Chinese ‘Magic Mirror’ That Projects Hidden Image Rediscovered After Decades in Museum Storage
Zhang said it would allow this ancient mural to re-enter contemporary cultural life, yet with all the context that great works of art carry with them as the centuries load up on their shoulders.
Other murals from Guangsheng, as it turns out, are located in American Museums—in Cincinnati and Missouri—both have which have already contacted Zhang for the purpose of examining the alignments and conditions of the works.

articles.content_orig:

The next meeting of the Kings County Historical Society will be held on Monday, Oct. 26, 2026, at 5:30 p.m.
The featured guest speaker will be Arianne Wing. Wing will speak on the future of China Alley. This will include an update on the restoration of the Taoist Temple Museum which was damaged by arson in May of 2021.
Wing is the President of the China Alley Preservation Society. She, along with her husband Steve Banister, who is the Society’s director of operations, recently received a grant to assist in that restoration.
Wing will provide details regarding the grant called the Placekeepers Fund from the Asian and Pacific Islander Americans in Historic Preservation (APIAHiP). It was granted along with support from the Mellon Foundation's Humanities in Place program.
The China Alley Preservation Society was one of 14 recipients selected nationwide for the inaugural Placekeepers Fund. There was a competitive pool of over 60 qualified applicants.
The grant is to be used specifically for the China Alley Taoist Temple Museum for interior reconstruction and remediation. The rear staircase will be rebuilt, and soot remediation will be completed. The interior of the museum suffered heavy smoke damage which destroyed numerous artifacts. Those that could be salvaged   required significant clean up and conservation efforts. China Alley is one of the last remaining rural Chinatowns in the country.
The Hong Kong Museum of History had long wanted to do an exhibit with artifacts from Hanford’s China Alley. This idea took shape around 2015.
The pandemic in 2020 created a roadblock to the project, and the arson fire in 2021 pretty much eliminated any hope of that. However, to Wing’s surprise, the museum still wanted to exhibit their artifacts. Those damaged by fire that could be saved were sent to Los Angeles and San Francisco to be conserved and restored.
It took a few years. Finally, on Nov. 27 of 2024, the Hanford China Alley exhibit opened at the Hong Kong Museum of History as part of the special Multifaceted Hong Kong' Exhibition Series exhibition titled "Sojourning in Gold Mountain – Hong Kong and the Lives of Overseas Chinese in California.”
The exhibit ended on June 7, 2026. Wing said that now that the exhibit is over it is time for the over 100 artifacts loaned to the Hong Kong Museum to return “home.” This will take place once the restoration of the Temple is completed.
Dr. Sonia Ng was guest curator of the Hong Kong Museum exhibit. She often discusses the topic of the Chinese migration to California via Hong Kong.
Wing said Ng first met Wing’s mother, Camille, in the mid-'80s. Ng worked closely with Camille and grew very fond of the history and artifacts of China Alley. Wing says Ng played a large part in the Hong Kong Museum wanting to exhibit the China Alley artifacts.
Wing and Banister have also recently submitted an application to the National Register of Historic Places.
You can enjoy Wing’s column, the Hanford Gourmet in The Sentinel every other Wednesday. She writes of the history of — and her love for — China Alley. Her columns always ends with a recipe.
Wing has been working on a new book. She will return to the Kings County Historical Society in early 2027 to do a reading and book signing after this latest title “In My Life, A Memoir of Hope and Gratitude” is published. The book picks up where her last book, “Disturbing the Dust,” left off. This book will contain columns and recipes like her last. Wing said that this book, written after Camille’s passing and the tragedy of the arson fire, will be about rebuilding after loss. How with the healing power of memory, hope can be found again.
As a nonprofit, the China Alley Preservation Society operates on donations from the community. Since the grant will cover the Taoist Temple Museum only, donations are still needed for the costs needed to operate and to complete the restoration of the rest of China Alley. If you would like to donate, please go to www.chinaalley.com
The Historical Society Dinner will begin at 5:30 p.m. Requested donation for the Chinese Cuisine dinner and presentation is $20. Please RSVP to Jackie Giacomazzi by Oct. 23, at jackiegiacomazzi@gmail.com or 559-816-0707.
There will be no meeting in November. Mark your calendar for Monday, Dec. 14, 2026, for the annual Historical Society Christmas Party.
The Kings County Historical Society Social Hall is located at 14060 Hackett Street in Hanford, near the corner of 14 th Avenue and Grangeville Blvd.
Donna Galletti covers art and culture for The Sentinel.

articles.title_orig: Putin, Trump and Xi Could Meet in China Next Month in High-Stakes Three-Way Summit
articles.title_zh: Putin, Trump and Xi Could Meet in China Next Month in High-Stakes Three-Way Summit
articles.content_orig:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has reportedly floated a three-way summit between himself, U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping to negotiate an end to the war in Ukraine, without Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy at the table.
The meeting was mentioned in a phone call to Trump on Oct. 9, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday, citing a former Russian intelligence officer briefed on the matter. Such a summit may take place at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in November in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, according to the report.
The call also produced a deal for Moscow to sell diesel on the global market.
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said early Monday that "there's been talks of a meeting. I don't know whether it's been finalized, but the president has been clear," he said in comments reported by Reuters.
"The president is open to anything that he can do to help bring a war to an end, if it's possible, and we'll continue to look for opportunities to do that," Rubio told reporters during a visit to Uzbekistan.
It comes amid mounting tensions between Ukraine and the U.S., its largest military backer. Over the past week, a series of moves by the Trump administration has raised fresh questions about Washington's reliability as Kyiv's most important military partner. It caused alarm among European allies and prompted criticism from fellow Republicans.
Over the weekend, Trump defended his decision to temporarily lift sanctions on Russian diesel exports, as well as an executive order on Oct. 18 to waive new Russia sanctions from a bill introduced by the late Senator Lindsey Graham.
Trump and Zelenskyy have traded criticism over how to end the war in Ukraine, with Trump accusing the Ukrainian president of not wanting peace , while Zelenskyy has argued that Washington's easing of sanctions on Russia risks prolonging the conflict. In a post on X, Zelenskyy said that ″the decision to undo all of this, to block all of it, seems wrong to me."
The tensions come as Russia launched another wave of overnight attacks on Ukraine, firing 16 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and the surrounding region and more than 200 drones across the country, according to Zelenskyy.
In a post on X on Monday, Zelenskyy said the strikes damaged more than 10 energy infrastructure facilities, leaving at least 550,000 households without power. He also said Ukraine had once again received no advance warning from its partners about the missile attacks. Casualties were reported, while a medical clinic, school, metro station and residential buildings were also damaged.
Ukraine's First Deputy Minister for Recovery, Infrastructure and Transport Serhiy Derkach told CNBC on Monday that Kyiv still hoped to retain Washington's support despite the growing tensions.
Asked whether the Trump administration was abandoning Ukraine and siding with Russia, Derkach said he did not believe the U.S. was abandoning Kyiv, but stressed that Ukraine hoped Washington would continue helping it or at least "stay in the middle."
"That's most important for us actually, not to lose the support of the U.S.," he said.
Russia has also intensified attacks on Ukraine's transport infrastructure, including road border crossings, railways and shipping routes, Derkach said.
It comes after Trump told Ukraine to stop striking Russian energy infrastructure, claiming that it was driving up global diesel prices.
Despite an "energy ceasefire" announced by Trump on Oct. 11, Russia continued striking Ukrainian infrastructure. Kyiv paused its attacks for three days before resuming them last Thursday, citing continued Russian strikes.
"America should see that Russia is not taking any reciprocal steps in response to sanctions relief or agreements. On the contrary, they take every signal of an opportunity to make money as proof that their bet on war is paying off and they can keep fighting," the Ukrainian president wrote on Sunday.
On Sunday, he also told Bloomberg that "steps have been taken to convince Ukraine to capitulate."
"I am not saying that this is the goal our partners are pursuing. I don't want to think that our American partners believe the war" against Russia "could be ended sooner at Ukraine's expense. But that's how it looks."
Over the weekend, both Kyiv and Moscow traded strikes, with Ukraine launching a strike of over 1,000 drones into Russia, setting fires at an oil export terminal and refinery in the city of St. Petersburg, while Moscow pounded Kyiv with ballistic missiles.
Last week, Kyiv also accused Washington of ordering restrictions on its Starshield networks, the military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink. Ukraine relies on this connectivity to track and intercept incoming threats.
SpaceX CEO Elon Musk pinned responsibility for any restrictions on the U.S. government and Trump, writing on X that "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the U.S. government."
Trump denied on Friday that the White House had ordered restrictions on Starlink satellite internet services provided to Ukraine's armed forces, after Reuters reported on Thursday that the call to restrict Starlink in Ukraine came from someone inside the White House, citing two U.S. officials.
The Telegraph reported on Friday that Musk "approached Donald Trump with the idea of slowing down Starlink in Ukraine," and both had a hand in imposing the restrictions.
Additionally, Zelenskyy told NBC's Meet the Press on Sunday that intelligence sharing between the two countries had been interrupted, but later "de-blocked."
Rubio on Monday denied that Washington had suspended intelligence sharing with Ukraine, contradicting Zelenskyy's claim that the flow of information had been briefly interrupted, Reuters reported.
Speaking to reporters in Uzbekistan, Rubio insisted there had been no pause and said Zelenskyy should instead focus on ending the war, marking another public disagreement between Washington and Kyiv amid deteriorating relations.

articles.title_orig: Exclusive / Saudi postpones FII in person after Wall Street lobbying
articles.title_zh: Exclusive / Saudi postpones FII in person after Wall Street lobbying
articles.content_orig:
Saudi Arabia has canceled in-person attendance at its flagship investment conference in Riyadh after Wall Street executives privately relayed safety concerns to organizers, including the boss of the kingdomâs sovereign wealth fund, people familiar with the matter said. Organizers of the Future Investment Initiative, due to take place next week, have dropped plans for a gathering of global and regional chief executives, and are telling delegates the event is postponed until 2027, the people said, confirming a Semafor story that a decision to postpone would be made today. The conference, which has become informally known as âDavos in the Desert,â is Saudi Arabiaâs highest profile event, attended by some of the biggest names in global finance and business. Next weekâs edition had been set to host JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon, Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon, and BlackRock CEO Larry Fink. Big banks and private equity firms had been privately relaying safety concerns about attending FII to Yasir Al-Rumayyan, Semafor reported earlier, according to people familiar with the matter.
Multiple signals suggested FII could be postponed: Rooms at the Ritz Carlton in Riyadh, which is usually blocked for the event, have been available for public booking in the past 24 hours. Other scheduled events such as an exhibition tennis tournament, a charity event linked to the crown prince, and Riyadh Fashion Week have all been postponed after the Houthis escalated attacks on the kingdom.
Delaying the conference is not surprising as the airport appears to still be closed, the main business district has instructed tenants to work from home until further notice, and schools have also shifted to home learning.
The kingdom, and its neighbors like the UAE and Qatar, have pitched themselves as not just sources of capital, but as a safe home for trillions in financial assets, data centers, and new industries.
Speculation has swirled in recent weeks over whether Saudi Arabia would go forward with the event, given high-profile attacks on the Riyadh airport. Organizers have held discussions around allowing overseas executives to participate virtually , Reuters reported last week, and The Wall Street Journal said that some executives had already canceled meetings .
The US, along with most other Western governments, recommends against all but essential travel to Saudi Arabia. That has knock-on effects on travel insurance costs and advice from internal security and risk teams.
Still, Saudi Arabia has viewed attendance at the event, and general support for the Gulf during turbulent times, as a loyalty test for global business leaders. Those who show up in tough times are rewarded, while fair-weather friends are often excluded from lucrative deals .
This story has been updated to reflect FIIâs decision to cancel the in-person meeting.

articles.title_orig: 3 waves of Russian missiles slam Kyiv overnight, killing at least 1, injuring 8
articles.title_zh: 3 waves of Russian missiles slam Kyiv overnight, killing at least 1, injuring 8
articles.content_orig:
Metro workers repair tracks damaged in a Russian attack in Kyiv, Ukraine, on Oct. 19, 2026. (Chris Occhicone/The Kyiv Independent)
Editor's note: This is a developing story and is being updated.
At least one person was killed and eight others injured after multiple waves of Russian missiles struck Kyiv overnight on Oct. 19.
Several explosions rocked the capital just before 11 p.m., with further attacks around 3 a.m. and 7 a.m., Kyiv Independent journalists on the ground reported. Ukraine's State Emergency Service (DSNS) said damage was reported in at least three districts.
One person was killed in the Desnianskyi District where a non-residential building caught fire and a metro station was damaged, DSNS said. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko earlier reported a fatality was that of 21-year-old woman.
The above-ground Chernihivska and Lisova metro stations were temporarily closed for repairs, city officials said.
Later on Oct. 19, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said more than 70 workers were repairing the damaged metro infrastructure, with the most difficult work involving power supply and train control systems. Repairs had continued since overnight but were being slowed by air raid alerts, which forced crews to take shelter.
Train service between Lisova and Akademmistechko stations was expected to resume that evening, with trains skipping Chernihivska until repairs were completed, Klitschko added.
Five people were injured in the Solomianskyi District when a 25-story residential building was damaged, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported. It is not yet clear where the other injuries occurred.
Допис, поширений Kyiv Independent (@kyivindependent_official)
The Cosmo Multimall shopping and entertainment center sustained significant damage in the Solomianskyi District. Its administration said no employees were injured and that the mall was working to resume operations as soon as possible. The center did not disclose the extent of the damage or provide a timeline for repairs.
Serhii Misan, 68, a local resident, had planned to pick up his new refrigerator from Cosmo Multimall on the morning of Oct. 19.
"I only paid for a refrigerator yesterday, and they told me I could pick it up today," Misan said. "And now look at what's happening here."
"(The Russians) are terrorists. They strike civilian targets. They spare no one — not children, not equipment, no one. They just kill civilians."
Misan added that, in light of recent developments, Ukraine would struggle to resist Russia without a strong partner like the U.S.
"If aid is reduced, it will be very difficult to stand up to an aggressor like Russia," he said. "We are not trying to seize their land. We are trying to defend our right to live freely on our own land."
Sofiia Kelli, 18, who lives in the Solomianskyi district, told The Kyiv Independent that her apartment was also damaged in the Russian attack on the capital. Her family was only able to take shelter in an underground parking garage after the attack began, as there was too little time between the air raid alert and the strikes.
"It was a huge shock. It was extremely loud — nothing like the other explosions we've heard in our neighborhood," Kelli said.
"I couldn't fall asleep afterward. Then I just sat in the bathroom and cried for a very long time. It's hard to process everything that happened because you always think something like this won't happen to you. And then it does."
"They [Russians] strike civilian targets. They [Russians] spare no one — not children, not equipment, no one. They [Russians] just kill civilians."
Kelli said she intends to stay in Kyiv despite the latest attack and is getting ready for the coming winter.
"Everything depends on electricity. Of course, it's difficult, but we're doing the best we can. We've installed solar panels (on the building) and a generator to keep the elevators running," she added.
Klitschko also reported damage to a medical center in the same district. The blast wave shattered more than 200 windows, damaged doors and ceilings, and damaged medical equipment, he said.
No medical center staff were injured, and there were no patients inside the facility at the time of the attack.
The Russian attack also destroyed a data center operated by telecommunications company Datagroup, which provides electronic communications services to users in more than 90 settlements across Ukraine.
The company said the facility's equipment and infrastructure had been damaged beyond repair. No employees were injured in the attack.
Russian attacks also hit settlements in Kyiv Oblast surrounding the capital. In Irpin, about 20 kilometers (12 miles) northwest of Kyiv, one woman was killed and 19 people were injured, including nine children.
At around 9 a.m. local time, Tymur Tkachenko , head of the Kyiv Regional Military Administration, said that three people were missing. Search operations are ongoing, he added.
The Russian strikes damaged 70 houses, five apartment buildings, industrial facilities, and warehouses in Irpin, according to Tkachenko.
Recent ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv have arrived with little or no advance warning amid deteriorating relations between Ukraine and the U.S., which provides intelligence used to track Russian missile launches.
President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed on the morning of Oct. 19 that Russian forces had attacked Ukraine with ballistic missiles, adding that Kyiv had received no advance warning from its partners about the launches.
According to Zelensky, Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles, with Kyiv and the surrounding region being the primary targets.
"When deliveries of missiles for Ukraine's air defense are blocked while Russia is granted relief or delays in sanctions, this is, unfortunately, a denial of reality on the part of our partners," Zelensky wrote on X.
"The reality is that the war continues, and it continues solely because of Russian strikes and Russia's desire to drag this war out."
Yurii Ihnat, head of the Ukrainian Air Force's communications department, said on national television that Russia launched two waves of ballistic missile attacks overnight on Oct. 19, at around 11 p.m. and 3 a.m. local time.
Ukraine received no advance warning from its partners ahead of the first wave, but information about the second wave was provided, Ihnat said.
He added that a similar situation had occurred during previous attacks, including the one overnight on Oct. 14.
"Information was indeed not provided the first time, for certain reasons. Our experts are looking into this together with our partners, as this is not the first time such a situation has occurred. Information was provided at 3 a.m.," Ihnat said.
"The 'warning' about a ballistic threat came through only after the strike had already happened."
Commenting on Ukrainian officials' claims that partners had not provided advance warning of Russia's ballistic missile launches overnight, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters on the morning of Oct. 19 that he "did not know exactly" what had happened.
"I know a few nights ago there was a software problem involving (Ukrainian) early warning system," Rubio said.
"I know that EUCOM (U.S. European Command) had been involved in looking at, and that's the report they gave us back.  I can't comment on what happened last night," he added.

Alerts did sound before the overnight strikes though the warnings were unusually short. The first explosions were simultaneous with the blaring of air raid sirens, according to Kyiv Independent journalists on the ground.
Phone alerts went off moments before the blasts, while the street sirens began "howling during the explosions," Chief Editor Olga Rudenko reported.
A senior Ukrainian official told the Kyiv Independent that the first overnight wave followed a similar pattern.

articles.title_orig: Micron, Intel lead chip recovery, adding nearly $250B as most of Wall Street falls: Chart of the Day
articles.title_zh: Micron, Intel lead chip recovery, adding nearly $250B as most of Wall Street falls: Chart of the Day
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Last week, chip stocks helped drag Wall Street lower. Monday, they're lifting the indexes while most stocks keep falling.
A Yahoo Finance basket of 60 chip-related stocks is recovering nearly $250 billion in market value, with gains reaching across memory makers, chip designers, and equipment suppliers.
Micron ( MU ) and Intel ( INTC ) are each gaining over 2%, while Sandisk ( SNDK ) is up nearly 5%. AMD ( AMD ), Nvidia ( NVDA ), and Western Digital ( WDC ) are joining the rebound.
Nearly 90% of the stocks in the chip basket are higher. Across the S&P 500, roughly 70% are falling, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.
The equal-weight S&P 500 ETF ( RSP ) is lower even as the main index advances, showing how much the headline recovery depends on a relatively small group of winners.
Many of those buyers are returning to familiar territory.
Micron and Sandisk lost roughly 15% and 18%, respectively, last week, as memory stocks entered another bear market . Both helped power the spring rally from the March lows as hopes of a US-Iran ceasefire improved.
That earlier leadership is showing up beyond individual chip names. Among the S&P 500's 100 strongest performers from March 30 through June 2 — the first big leg higher after war headlines faded — 61 are rising Monday. Among the 100 weakest, 84 are falling.
Intel also has a fresh catalyst. JPMorgan upgraded it to Neutral from Underweight, citing opportunities tied to AI demand and chip scarcity, as Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi reports .
The rebound is getting a tougher reception elsewhere in AI.
CoreWeave ( CRWV ) has surrendered most of its premarket gains despite a Goldman Sachs upgrade to Buy . The cloud provider's financing needs were front and center in last week's selling.
Semiconductor stocks have also pulled back since the open. For chip bulls, the PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) would ideally close above 11,500 today and needs to hold the 11,000-11,100 area to avoid a larger washout.

articles.title_orig: Elon Musk Says He Will Give a SpaceX Share to ‘Every Kid in America’
articles.title_zh: Elon Musk Says He Will Give a SpaceX Share to ‘Every Kid in America’
articles.content_orig:
SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said Monday that he'll give every child in the U.S. one of his shares in the company next year.
Musk currently owns about 4.8 billion SpaceX shares, according to an August SEC filing. That figure rises to 6.4 billion when taking into account unvested awards and stock options, representing a 48.4% beneficial stake in the company.
There were 72 million children under 18 in the U.S. as of July 1, 2025, according to official census data.
That would amount to the CEO giving away about $10.5 billion worth of shares, taking into account SpaceX's closing stock price of $146.03 as of Friday.
"This will be the first of many," Musk said in a post on X, without providing further details on how the share giveaway would happen.
CNBC has reached out to SpaceX and Musk's family office for further details.
The founder of Invest America, Trump Accounts and Altimeter Capital, Brad Gerstner, praised the move and suggested in a post on X that the SpaceX shares could be distributed via Trump accounts.
"Incredible Elon!" he wrote. "This will be the largest philanthropic gift in history! 70 M accounts - every citizen under 18 & every child born forevermore now has a free, lifetime investment acct making them an owner in the upside of America & our greatest companies!"
Musk's financial giving has been in the news in recent weeks primarily for his political contributions.
The Tesla CEO has spent more than $276 million in donations to Republican groups since July, making him the biggest known donor of the 2026 midterm election.
The world's richest person poured $158 million into the Senate Leadership Fund, the Republican Party's leading Senate super PAC, in September through an affiliated Texas PAC created to support Republican Ken Paxton. Musk's two contributions of $75 million and $83 million are among the largest political donations ever.
When it comes to fulfilling his philanthropic promises , Musk has a rocky track record.
For example, the Tesla and SpaceX CEO contributed about $38 million to OpenAI , which he co-founded as a nonprofit research lab, between 2016 and 2020. But he had promised to contribute up to $1 billion, and cut off donations to the organization amid a battle with cofounders for control of the company.
In 2021, Musk said he would donate $6 billion to the United Nations World Food Program if it could show him a plan for how they'd use the money to "solve world hunger." While the WFP posted a plan , Musk did not donate.
The tech multi-billionaire's foundation has also repeatedly fallen shy of making the minimum donations it's required to by law, and as New York Times previously reported, its donations go to charities that closely benefit Musk and his companies directly.
Musk's post came hot on the heels of Anthropic revealing that it plans to commit 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund, with the stake potentially increasing as the company's valuation grows.
In response to an Anthropic post on X about the fund on Sunday, Musk replied, "I recommend giving the shares directly to the public," and added that's what he'd be doing.
Subject to shareholder approval, Anthropic's fund would immediately commit 5% of Anthropic's shares, with the board adding, at its discretion, an additional 2% for every 50% increase in the company's value above a set baseline that has yet to be disclosed.
The fund may be used to "explore large donations," including to traditional nonprofits or as direct distributions for specific populations, or for "bolder approaches" to study and address AI's disruption and displacement of jobs, the company said.
— CNBC's Jennifer Liu contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: ‘GTA 6’ Will Face Something It Couldn’t Have Prepared For At Launch
articles.title_zh: ‘GTA 6’ Will Face Something It Couldn’t Have Prepared For At Launch
articles.content_orig:
Rockstar reportedly plans to release GTA 6 on PC during the first quarter of 2027.
GamesBeat reported the news based on four sources who asked to remain anonymous. Rockstar and parent company Take-Two are yet to comment.
If true, it would mean GTA 6 hitting PC just a few months after it launches on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S on November 19, 2026. Some had anticipated a longer wait for the game on PC, given it took nearly two years for GTA 5 to launch on PC after consoles.
The PC launch may tie into the release of GTA 6's multiplayer mode, which fans are calling GTA Online 2 while they wait for official word from Rockstar. While Rockstar has yet to confirm an online mode for GTA 6, last month Twitch boss Dan Clancy said GTA Online 2 — or whatever GTA 6’s multiplayer mode is called — will launch next year.
Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick has always responded with vague comments when asked about the prospect of launching GTA 6 on PC, pointing to Rockstar for announcements. In May, Zelnick told Bloomberg that Rockstar "always starts on console because I think with regard to a release like that you're judged by serving the core. Like really serving the core consumer. If your core consumer isn't there, if they're not served first and best, you kind of don't hit your other consumers.”
Red Dead Redemption, GTA 5, LA Noire, Max Payne 3, and Red Dead Redemption 2 all came to PC after consoles. And while GTA's core audience may be on console, it has a huge fanbase of active players on PC, fueled by GTA Online and role-play servers.
Indeed, 12 months ago, Zelnick said the industry was “moving towards PC,” telling CNBC’s Squawk Box that the video game business was trending towards “open rather than closed.”
In 2024, Zelnick was asked if the lack of a PC version of GTA 6 was set in stone . Here’s his response in full:
Assuming GTA 6 does come to PC early next year, one of the big questions players will have is how it runs compared to on consoles. Rockstar has yet to confirm the performance of GTA 6 on consoles, so we're still in the dark when it comes to frames-per-second and resolution. But the expectation is that any PC version would be capable of better performance, assuming your rig is powerful enough.

articles.title_orig: New nonstop Lufthansa flight announced from Columbus to Frankfurt
articles.title_zh: New nonstop Lufthansa flight announced from Columbus to Frankfurt
articles.content_orig:
Published: October 19, 2026
(COLUMBUS) The Columbus Regional Airport Authority, Lufthansa Airlines, JobsOhio and One Columbus today announced that Central Ohio's first nonstop flight to Europe will launch in May 2027, connecting John Glenn Columbus International Airport (CMH) with Frankfurt Airport (FRA) in Germany. The new service marks a major milestone for the Columbus Region and Ohio, providing direct access to one of the world's leading international hubs and creating new opportunities for businesses, travelers and visitors throughout the state.
“Today's announcement is a tremendous milestone for the Columbus Region and Ohio,” said Daren Griffin, CRAA President and CEO. “Lufthansa's new nonstop service to Frankfurt provides our passengers with a direct link to one of the world's strongest global networks, enhancing connectivity, competitiveness and continued growth. We are grateful to Lufthansa, JobsOhio, One Columbus, our business community and so many others whose partnership helped make this opportunity possible. At a time of extraordinary transformation for our airports and our region, this new service establishes Ohio's gateway to continental Europe. It strengthens our state's connections to the global economy and creates new opportunities for communities across Ohio. We couldn't be more excited about what it means for our businesses, travelers and the future of Ohio”
This will be Ohio's first and only nonstop flight to Germany, serving hundreds of daily passengers from Columbus and across Ohio who travel to Europe each day. Lufthansa will operate the service with a Boeing 787 Dreamliner featuring the airline's Allegris cabin experience, including 28 lie-flat business class seats, 28 premium economy seats and 231 economy seats, for a total of 287 seats.
“We are very pleased to connect Columbus and the state of Ohio directly with our Frankfurt hub, the first intercontinental flight from this great city,” said Dirk Janzen, Lufthansa Group Vice President of Passenger Sales, the Americas. “The new service will provide both business and leisure travelers with a convenient nonstop connection to Germany, as well as onward destinations across our Lufthansa Group network. The launch of this route is an important step in our continued expansion in the United States, our most important market outside the Lufthansa Group’s home markets. We look forward to strengthening the connections between Ohio and Europe, and to welcoming travelers from Columbus and the surrounding region,” Janzen added.
The flight will provide unprecedented connectivity for the 38 German-based companies operating in the Columbus Region and further support all German companies investing in Ohio and employing thousands of Ohioans across the state. Through Lufthansa's Frankfurt hub, travelers will have convenient access to more than 130 destinations across Europe, the Middle East, Africa and India.
The new service is also expected to make it easier for international visitors, investors and talent to access the Columbus Region and explore opportunities across Ohio, further supporting the state's economic development efforts.
“Ohio is committed to building a collaborative partnership with Lufthansa to support the success of this new route and strengthen the significant ties that benefit both of our regions,” said Ohio Governor Mike DeWine. “This new route will be transformative, giving our state access to critical markets in Germany, Europe and the world while establishing stronger economic, research, cultural and educational exchanges.”
Germany is the third-largest source of international investment in Ohio, behind only Japan and Canada. More than 750 German-owned business establishments operate in Ohio, second only to Japan, according to the Ohio Department of Development, and German companies support approximately 41,000 jobs across the state, according to the Transatlantic Economy 2025 report. Ohio businesses also exported nearly $1.4 billion in goods to Germany in 2023. Overall, Ohio ranks third in the nation for foreign direct investment, with about 4,000 companies from 42 countries operating in the state.
The new route builds on the success of JobsOhio’s Air Service Restoration program, which works with airports, regional partners and airlines to establish routes that are important to economic development. JobsOhio created the program after businesses and stakeholders said during a 2019 statewide listening tour that air service at Ohio airports had declined more sharply than in competitor states. Through the program, JobsOhio and regional partners share revenue guarantees that reduce the risk for airlines launching new service.
Since 2020, it has helped bring 32 new routes and 15 route expansions with six airlines to five Ohio airports, adding more than 590,000 new seats and more than 187,000 additional seats each year and generating an estimated $230 million in annual economic impact. JobsOhio has committed $36.8 million in revenue guarantees, alongside $10.1 million from local partners.
“Businesses, including the German companies that employ tens of thousands of Ohioans, tell us that better air service is essential to investing and creating jobs in Ohio,” said JobsOhio President and CEO J.P. Nauseef. “We listened, and this direct link to Frankfurt is exactly what our Air Service Restoration program was built to deliver.”
The new air service comes as the Columbus Region experiences some of the strongest economic growth in the country. The Columbus metro leads the Midwest in job creation, adding nearly 12,000 jobs between March 2025 and March 2026, with a growth rate more than 18 times the national average. The Region’s population also grew by more than 21,000 residents in 2025, twice the national growth rate. The new international connection is expected to further strengthen the Region’s ability to attract businesses, investment and talent from around the world.
“The Columbus Region is in the middle of an extraordinary stretch of job creation and business investment, and now we’re adding direct access to one of Europe’s most important business hubs,” said Jonas Peterson, Chief Economic Development Officer and President of One Columbus. “That’s a significant competitive advantage. It makes it easier for global companies to invest here, strengthens connections for businesses already operating in our Region and improves our ability to compete for the next major project. We have tremendous economic momentum right now, and this new connection gives us an opportunity to accelerate it even further.”
The Columbus Region continues to attract global investment and advanced industries, including recent commitments from companies such as Anduril, Intel and Bayer. The new Lufthansa service further strengthens Ohio's position as a destination for business growth and international commerce.
The CMH-FRA route will begin operating in May 2027, with bookings available beginning Tuesday, Oct. 20. Service will operate three times weekly on Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays. Flights will depart Columbus at 4:20 p.m. and arrive in Frankfurt at 6:15 a.m. (local times).
The Lufthansa Group is a globally operating aviation group, with more than 100,000 employees worldwide. It is Europe's largest airline group by revenue, generating revenue of EUR 39.6 billion (EUR 39,597 million) in the 2025 financial year. The Lufthansa Group comprises mulitple business segments, including Passenger Airlines, Logistics, Technology (Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul), as well as other companies and group functions, including IT services and Lufthansa Aviation Training.
The Lufthansa Group’s portfolio of airlines includes Lufthansa, SWISS, Austrian Airlines, Brussels Airlines, ITA Airways, Eurowings and Discover Airlines, connecting customers to destinations around the globe. articles.title_orig: Rabbi Shmuel Yitzchak Malov, 51, OBM
articles.title_zh: Rabbi Shmuel Yitzchak Malov, 51, OBM
articles.content_orig:
Rabbi Shmuel Yitzchak Malov , a longtime educator and respected member of the Chabad community in Nachlas Har Chabad, Kiryat Malachi, passed away suddenly on Monday morning. Full Story
Rabbi Shmuel Yitzchak Malov , a longtime educator and respected member of the Chabad community in Nachlas Har Chabad, Kiryat Malachi, passed away suddenly on Monday morning. Full Story
Rabbi Shmuel Yitzchak Malov , a beloved educator and longtime member of the Chabad community in Nachlas Har Chabad, Kiryat Malachi, passed away suddenly on Monday, 8 Cheshvan, 5787.
Rabbi Malov suffered a sudden cardiac arrest shortly after waking up and washing Negel Vasser. Emergency responders were called to his home but were unable to revive him.
His sudden passing has shocked the Chabad community in Nachlas Har Chabad and his many friends and acquaintances throughout Israel and around the world.
Rabbi Malov served as the Rebbe’s Shliach in Kfar HaRif and dedicated much of his life to Jewish education. For many years, he directed the neighborhood’s evening yeshiva program, where hundreds of children gathered nightly in the local shul to study Torah.
Friends described him as a devoted educator and accomplished Torah scholar, knowledgeable in both Nigleh and Chassidus, who worked tirelessly to spread Torah learning.
He also organized annual Kinusei Torah in the neighborhood around Yom Tov, in accordance with the Rebbe’s directive to hold Torah gatherings during the holidays.
Rabbi Malov was the son-in-law of Rabbi Yitzchak Yehuda Yeruslavsky , Rov of Nachlas Har Chabad and a leading Chabad Rov.
He was born in Bnei Brak to Rabbi Tzvi Eliyahu Malov , OBM, a longtime Chabad communal activist in Yerushalayim who passed away approximately six years ago, and Mrs. Chana Chaya Malov , daughter of R’ Yaakov Moshe Hakohen Halperin , who passed away in Tishrei 5751 at the age of 40.
He is survived by his wife, Mrs. Nechama Dina Malov , and their children: Menachem Mendel, Shterna Sarah Kramer, Devorah Leah , and Mushka .
The levaya will depart from his home in Nachlas Har Chabad at 12:30 PM, passing the local Talmud Torah and central shul before proceeding to Shamgar in Yerushalayim.
The levaya will depart Shamgar at 3:00 PM for burial at Har Hamenuchos in Yerushalayim.

The Final Porta weigh just 40 grams and offer up to eight hours of battery life.﻿
The Final Porta weigh just 40 grams and offer up to eight hours of battery life.﻿
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
If you’re on the hunt for lightweight wireless headphones but wearing earbuds or clip-ons never feels comfortable or secure, a relatively obscure Japanese headphone maker could have the solution. Final’s new Porta headphones feature an on-ear design supported by a headband but with a structure made from a single piece of wire so they weigh just 40 grams. For comparison, Marshall’s recently-launched Milton A.N.C. are also designed to be smaller on-ear headphones but weigh 200 grams.
The Final Porta are available for preorder now through the company’s online store for 12,800 yen (around $80) with black or orange ear pads and shipping expected to start on October 23rd. The company also has an Amazon shop for US-based customers, but the Porta aren’t listed there yet.
Sporting a design that looks loosely inspired by the lightweight headphones Sony bundled with its Walkmans decades ago, the Porta’s functionality is unsurprisingly basic. A 57mAh battery charges over USB-C and provides up to eight hours of use while the Porta are wirelessly paired to a device using Bluetooth 5.4 and streaming audio over the SBC and AAC codecs. There’s no active noise cancelation which is not uncommon for on-ear headphones that don’t create a full seal, but with an IPX4 rating you should be able to use the Porta in the rain or while working up a sweat without worrying about them getting damaged by the moisture.

articles.title_orig: 10 Mini Gadgets Worth 3D Printing Instead Of Buying
articles.title_zh: 10 Mini Gadgets Worth 3D Printing Instead Of Buying
articles.content_orig:
If you're thinking about buying a 3D printer , you should know that there's no limit to the things that you can make once you get one. While everyone has probably thought about making large pieces, printing smaller items could also result in lots of saved time and money.
For this article, we identified 10 mini gadgets worth 3D printing instead of buying, and we've given some examples for each of them so you can see the benefits. Some of our selections for this roundup include stands and docks for mobile devices, an alternative to keychains, and accessories for tabletop games.
All of the examples that we've included are publicly available from the best sites for free 3D printing projects , though some of them come with the restriction that you can only make them for personal use. They've all been downloaded at least 1,000 times, though, so it's likely the creators have received plenty of feedback and maybe even updated their files as needed to address any concerns raised.
When you buy an Apple Watch , there's no charging stand that comes with it. You'll only get a charging puck, so the smartwatch lies flat on your desk. You can buy a charging stand that holds the watch upright so that you can see the time and notifications, but most options in the market are expensive because they come with extras like wireless charging capabilities or additional space for your iPhone and AirPods. 3D printing this gadget will not only save on costs, but you'll also be able to choose the color that you want.
If you want something simple, there are 3D-printed options like the Apple Watch Charging Stand by Dan_ID on Maker World. With about 59,500 downloads, it holds the smartwatch's charging puck and sets the Apple Watch horizontally with the straps wrapped around it to minimize the space that it occupies on your desk.
Pulsar Designs' Charging Stand for Apple Watch , also available on Maker World and with 13,300 downloads, sets the wearable device vertically instead. This design also holds the charging puck securely, and it's compact while also elevating the smartwatch for a better look at the straps that you chose for the day.
Similar to the Apple Watch charging stand, a phone dock will allow you to see your smartphone's screen at all times, whether it's plugged into its charger or not. These accessories come in all shapes and sizes, but 3D printing one will allow you to choose the exact style that you want depending on how much space you have available on your desk and the size of your phone.
The Phone Stand by GoAftens on Thingiverse is as simple as it gets for this type of accessory. With about 40,100 downloads and originally made for Apple's iPhone 6, it has a hole at the bottom to allow a charging cable to plug into your phone while it's placed vertically on the stand, though you also have the option of setting it horizontally. You can adjust the width of the ledge if you've got a thick phone, such as a foldable, or because your preferred case is bulky.
Moss 3D's Adjustable Phone Stand , which has about 2,500 downloads on Maker World, is a slightly more modern version of the gadget. It's foldable for portability, and you can set it at a variety of angles to suit your needs. It features a locking function to keep it in place even when it's holding a heavier device like a tablet. With its retro aesthetic and your choice of colors for its parts, this phone stand also has more personality than many of the other options in the market.
Toothpaste squeezers are essential for frugal living, and it goes against the principles of the lifestyle if the gadget that you buy costs a lot, breaks easily, or isn't effective. 3D-printed toothpaste squeezers are not only tried and tested, but you'll also be able to make the exact number that you need, in the specific size for your usual toothpaste tubes.
The Toothpaste Squeezer by mgm86, which has been downloaded 28,500 times from Maker World, gives a more precise and direct squeeze than many similar gadgets that have a fixed slot. To use it, you remove the colored cap to insert the toothpaste tube, then re-insert the cap to tighten the grip and further flatten the tube. There are two sizes available for the project, one with a slot length of 58 millimeters and the other at 68 millimeters. You can also customize the colors of the caps depending on the household member who's using each particular brand of toothpaste.
The Ultimate Toothpaste Squeezer by the pro is another option, but it uses rollers to get every drop out of the tube instead of relying on direct pressure from your hands. Downloaded about 20,000 times on Printables, this gadget has a wheel for turning the gears and squeezing the toothpaste tube. It may look complicated, but assembly after 3D printing won't require additional tools, and it can be disassembled for thorough cleaning if necessary.
There are a lot of types of fidget toys you can buy , as they've evolved from just being simple spinners. You can now also click and squeeze them, among many other actions, with the goal of either keeping your mind focused or relieving your stress. If you're still figuring out what kind of fidget toy works the best for you, or if you already know and you want different versions of your favorites, you can 3D print them so that you can customize their size and colors.
Kriswillcode's Mechanical Switch Fidget Click Toy , which has 1,600 downloads on Thingiverse, mimics the feel and sound of typing on a mechanical keyboard. In addition to seven 3D-printed pieces that need to be accurately sized, you'll need a spring like those in retractable pens to assemble this gadget. If done right, you'll get a satisfying click each time you press its button.
For a different kind of fidget toy, there's the Tactile Fidget Rings by GlennovitS 3D. You can get its files from Printables, where it has been downloaded about 42,000 times. This is a print-in-place project, which means there's no assembly necessary after 3D printing, and there are a total of five options for the textures of the rotating rings. There are also four mixed versions that have a different texture for each ring, and of course, you can choose the color that you want when you print them for yourself or to give to your friends and family members.
Open bag clips are very useful in the kitchen, as they help keep food and ingredients fresh by allowing you to reseal the packages. However, when you buy these accessories, they usually come in bundles of different sizes, where some are too big or small, or there are so many that you won't be able to use them all. If you 3D print your open bag clips instead, you're going to get the specific size and quantity that you need, and you can even make them part of a color-coded system in your refrigerator or pantry.
The Crazy Crocodile Clip , made by Newstream and downloaded about 5,700 times on Maker World, is a 3D-printable open bag clip that resembles a crocodile, as its name suggests. It's more than just a fun design, though, as the accessory can keep packages sealed securely. This latest version of the project has a stronger print-in-place hinge for durability than earlier iterations, and as its creator suggested, it can even double as a fidget toy.
Coffee Clip for Open Bags , which has about 24,000 downloads on Printables, adds a resealable cap to the open bag clip for easy pouring of whatever's inside. Pressi, the designer of the 3D-printed gadget, said that it can be used for coffee beans, snacks, spices, and other similar food items in lightweight packages.
If you're always misplacing your keys, a key organizer can help make sure that they're all in one place. Some key organizers are shaped to keep all your keys together for better portability, while others serve as storage for easy access to everyone in the family. When you buy this gadget, you need to check if there's enough space for all your keys, but if you 3D print it, you'll get one with the exact specifications that you need.

articles.title_orig: A hacker broke into John Deere and SharkNinja with an army of AI agents
articles.title_zh: A hacker broke into John Deere and SharkNinja with an army of AI agents
articles.content_orig:
The AI agents carried out the attacks with little involvement from the human hacker.
The AI agents carried out the attacks with little involvement from the human hacker.
A hacker broke into more than 100 websites using an army of AI agents that mostly operated on their own, according to findings from the AI security firm Norforge . Though Norforge doesn’t name the targets, Reuters reports that the victims included companies like John Deere, SharkNinja, and Cummins.
Concerns over AI-powered cybersecurity breaches have grown as the technology grows more advanced, with hackers using the tools to carry out large-scale attacks. At the same time, rogue AI agents are carrying out attacks of their own after escaping from testing environments.
Researchers at Norforge uncovered the attacks through exposed work on Cairn, an open-source AI platform that describes itself as a “general-purpose problem-solving engine.” With Cairn, users set a start and end point for the AI agents, which document their progress as they move forward with the task. However, as noted by Norforge, hackers can also use the tool to orchestrate cyberattacks using AI agents.
The hacker who broke into more than 100 sites was the “most active” among the exposed Cairn instances discovered by Norforge, waging attacks on companies based in the US, Canada, Australia, and Japan, as reported by Reuters . This attacker laid out “preferred intrusion tactics” using fewer than 100 Chinese characters, with successful breaches taking about 23 hours, according to Reuters . Overall, Nordforge found more than 20 exposed Cairn instances that are “likely malicious.”
In a statement to Reuters , a John Deere spokesperson said there is “no indication that ​sensitive information was accessed” as a result of the attack, while Cummins said it’s “investigating the report of a potential cyber-attack on a website operated by one of our third-party vendors.”
Meanwhile, SharkNinja says the breach impacted a standalone site with product support information, and that it has contained the threat. John Deere, Cumms, and SharkNinja didn’t immediately respond to The Verge ’s request for comment.
Nordforge says it’s working to get the malicious Cairn instances taken down. Cairn’s creator, who goes by @le1xia0, said earlier this month that the platform “was never a ‘hacking tool,’” adding that “misuse is a human decision, not a feature of the engine.”

articles.title_orig: Saudi Arabia executes 2 Bangladeshis over ‘indecent acts,’ and other Mideast news
articles.title_zh: Saudi Arabia executes 2 Bangladeshis over ‘indecent acts,’ and other Mideast news
articles.content_orig:
Bangladeshi authorities say they were not informed of the recent execution of two Bangladeshi nationals in the holy city of Mecca until after it had taken place, local media reports.
A Bangladeshi man and woman were executed last Wednesday after being convicted of committing an "indecent act" inside a mosque, according to the Saudi interior ministry. The ministry did not specify the nature of the offending act.
Bangladesh says it has reached out to the Saudi Arabian government to ask for more details about the case.
The two Muslim countries share a close relationship due to their religious affinity and strong economic ties.
More than three million Bangladeshis work and live in Saudi Arabia, mostly in low-paying jobs, and news of the double execution has raised public concern in Bangladesh.
According to the Saudi interior ministry, the two Bangladeshi nationals were convicted and sentenced to death under "tazir", which in Islamic law refers to punishments left to the discretion of the judge.
The ministry statement said they were handed the sentences because of the severity of the offence, and the fact that they violated the "sanctity" of the mosque.
Bangladesh has reached out to the Saudi government about the offences involved and legal proceedings in the case, said state minister for foreign affairs Shama Obaed Islam.
The government would consider next steps, such as the repatriation of the bodies, after getting information from Saudi authorities, Islam said.
She added that the government was committed to safeguarding the welfare and interests of Bangladeshis abroad.
The two executed Bangladeshis were included in a list of prisoners that Saudi Arabia had shared with Bangladesh, upon a request from the Bangladesh Consulate General in Jeddah - but that list did not indicate that the pair had been sentenced to death, the Daily Star reported.
This is not the first time that foreign nationals have been executed by Saudi authorities.
According to Amnesty International, the country has executed around 100 people this year, many of whom are foreigners convicted of drug offences.
In 2011, eight Bangladeshi men were publicly executed in the Saudi Arabian capital of Riyadh after they were found guilty of killing an Egyptian.
Earlier this month, Saudi Arabia overturned a death sentence handed to a Sri Lankan man over a comment he had made on Facebook, which had led to him being convicted of blasphemy. That decision came after the case sparked public outcry in Sri Lanka and spurred diplomatic efforts to seek clemency for the man.

A Massachusetts company recalled more than 1.5 million pounds of ready-to-eat meat and poultry products that were produced over the past eight months after determining that they may not have been stored properly.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture posted the recall by Kayem Foods Inc., along with a list of scores of affected products. In addition to its own branded products, Kayem pulled items made under Al Fresco, McKenzie, and multiple other brands. (See lists below.)
The recalled products were manufactured over an eight-month span that stretches from March 31, 2026, to Oct. 7, 2026, and sent to stores and food service companies across the United States, as well as in Hong Kong, the statement on the USDA website indicated.
The affected items will have the establishment numbers "EST. M/P 7839," "EST. P 20935A" and "EST. M 9520" inside the USDA mark of inspection, it noted. See slideshow for images of the packaging of the recalled products.
RELATED: New protein ranking names unexpected winner over beef, salmon and eggs
The USDA released images of the packages subject to a recall by Kayem Foods Inc. of approximately 1.5 million pounds of meat products and included brands such as AlFresco, Kayem, and McKenzie, among others. (Source: USDA)
The USDA website explained that the recall was triggered after a customer complained about a product being warm when it was delivered at the beginning of October. An investigation revealed that some of the company’s meat and poultry products were stored in a warehouse cooler where the temperature had deviated from where it was supposed to be.
While the USDA is not aware of any illnesses linked to the products, its Food Safety and Inspection Service is concerned that the items may still be sitting in customers’ refrigerators. It advises anyone who finds one of the packages to throw it out or return it to its place of purchase.
